answer_text:
Let \(B=A^2\). Since \(A\) is real symmetric, by the spectral theorem

\[
A=Q\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n)Q^T,\qquad \lambda_i\in\mathbb{R}.
\]

Hence

\[
A^2=Q\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1^2,\dots,\lambda_n^2)Q^T,
\]

so the eigenvalues of \(A^2\) are \(\lambda_i^2\ge 0\).

For the linear system \(\dot x=A^2x\), the zero solution is Lyapunov stable only if all eigenvalues of \(A^2\) have nonpositive real parts. Since all eigenvalues here are nonnegative, they must all be zero. Thus

\[
\lambda_i^2=0 \quad \forall i \implies \lambda_i=0 \quad \forall i,
\]

so \(A=0\).

Conversely, if \(A=0\), then \(\dot x=0\), so solutions remain constant and the zero solution is stable.

\[
\boxed{A=0_{n\times n}}
\]
